title: Thracian Kingdom
capsule: The Thracian Kingdom attested in this dataset (c. 87 BCE – 51 CE) corresponds to the Sapaean client monarchy of Thrace, whose capital was at Bizye (modern Vize, northwestern Turkey) and which emerged as a dominant power in the region following the Odrysian kingdoms' decline. King Rhoemetalces I (c. 11 BCE–12 CE) governed as a loyal Roman auxiliary, suppressing Thracian tribal revolts on Rome's behalf after the Battle of Actium (31 BCE); his death triggered civil war between his son Cotys III and brother Rhescuporis II. Repeated dynastic conflicts weakened the kingdom; after Rhoemetalces III was killed in a revolt around 44/45 CE, Emperor Claudius annexed Thrace as a Roman province in 46 CE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Broad parameters of the kingdom are attested in Roman literary sources and numismatics; precise territorial limits are difficult to establish as the kingdom's control of different Thracian tribal confederacies fluctuated, and the dataset's from date of 87 BCE is earlier than the canonical Sapaean period.
